content.value_statement: Long AI sessions can waste tokens and lose important state. This skill provides practical tactics for budgeting, masking, compaction, caching, and partitioning.
actual_capabilities: Recommends when to use masking, compaction, KV-cache optimization, or partitioning.
Defines token budget categories and threshold-based optimization triggers.
Provides rules for preserving critical state during compaction.
Explains how stable prompt prefixes improve cache hit rates.
Includes reference code for token estimates, masking, budgets, and cache metrics.
limitations: Token estimates use simple heuristics unless connected to a model tokenizer.
Compaction guidance still requires validation against task quality goals.
Partitioning advice works best when subtasks are independent.
The included scripts are demonstration utilities, not a full production service.

use_cases.title: Control Long Coding Sessions
use_cases.description: Reduce context bloat while keeping current goals, errors, and decisions available.

use_cases.title: Lower AI Operations Cost
use_cases.description: Design stable prefixes and token budgets for repeated agent workflows.

use_cases.title: Plan Multi-Agent Work
use_cases.description: Split large tasks across focused contexts when one window cannot hold the work.

prompt_templates.title: Check Context Budget
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review before a long task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current task context. Identify the largest token categories and suggest one safe optimization to apply first.

prompt_templates.title: Mask Old Observations
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate cleanup after several tool-heavy turns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find verbose observations that are no longer active. Replace each with a short reference, key summary, and retrieval note.

prompt_templates.title: Design Cache-Stable Prompts
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt structure review for repeated requests.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this prompt layout for KV-cache stability. Move dynamic fields later and list changes that improve prefix reuse.

prompt_templates.title: Partition a Large Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for work that exceeds one context window.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a context partitioning plan for this task. Define subtasks, coordinator responsibilities, merge checks, and token overhead risks.

output_examples.input: A session has many old tool outputs and is near the context limit.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends masking resolved outputs first, then compacting remaining history once critical state is preserved.

output_examples.input: A repeated support workflow has high prompt cost and similar requests.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests stable system and template prefixes, with dynamic metadata moved near the end of the request.

output_examples.input: A research task requires several independent document reviews.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends partitioning by document group and merging structured summaries through a coordinator.

best_practices: Measure token usage and quality before applying optimization.
Mask low-value observations before lossy compaction.
Validate summaries against current goals after every compaction.
anti_patterns: Do not compress the system prompt or active user constraints.
Do not hide recent errors during active debugging.
Do not partition small tasks where coordination costs exceed savings.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps reduce wasted context while preserving the information needed for high-quality AI work.

faq.question: Does it replace a tokenizer?
faq.answer: No. It gives planning guidance and simple estimates, but production systems should use model-specific tokenizers.

faq.question: When should I compact context?
faq.answer: Use compaction after masking low-value bulk, especially when utilization approaches the defined threshold.

faq.question: When is masking unsafe?
faq.answer: Masking is unsafe when content is recent, central to reasoning, or needed for active debugging.

faq.question: How does this help Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: It gives both tools a structured way to keep long sessions focused and token efficient.

faq.question: Can it improve cache hit rates?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to keep stable prompt content at the beginning and move dynamic content later.
